https://www.penbaypilot.com:443/article/.text: Visit our partners: Boothbay Register Wiscasset Newspaper Search form Wed, 07/29/2026 - 2:28pm Josephine Pitts McAlary Josephine Pitts McAlary A life very well lived ROCKPORT — Jojo McAlary passed away peacefully at Wingate Residences, in Haverhill, Massachusetts, her “home away from home” for the last two and a half years, surrounded by family and friends, after a short period of declining health on July 21, 2026. She was two weeks short of her 103 rd birthday. Born August 8, 1923 in New Orleans, Louisiana, the only child of Everett E. Pitts and Diana Wall Pitts (later Fogler). She lived in New Orleans until 1937 when the family moved back to the family home in Rockport, Maine. Jojo was in a class of nine that graduated from Rockport High School in 1940. She went on to attend Colby College, graduating in December 1943. She met her future husband, Frederick McAlary, at Colby College and they were married two hours after she received her diploma on December 12, 1943. Frederick, also a Colby graduate was in the U.S. Army at that time. He was soon deployed to Europe during WWII, not returning until the Fall of 1945. In his absence Jojo lived in Rockport, taught high school and gave birth to their first child, Diana. After being discharged from the Army, they moved to Bangor, Maine where Fred began a 38 year career with the Bangor Daily News. In 1947 they had a second child, Fred, Jr. In addition to bringing up her young family, Jojo was active with the womens’ group at St. John’s Episcopal Church, scouting clubs, Lionetts and Patawa Club. In 1963, she returned to teaching in the Math Department at Fifth Street Junior High School. In 1972 she transferred to Bangor High School where she taught algebra and geometry, was a class advisor and was very active many school activities. She and Fred both retired in 1985. After retiring they moved into the Rockport house that they had inherited from her parents which became their year-round home. Traveling annually became a passion; Europe to celebrate D-Day’s 50th anniversary, Australia, New Zealand, Florida and many Caribbean islands. In 2004, after several years of failing health Fred passed shortly after their 60th anniversary. Jojo decided that Rockport would remain her forever home where she was surrounded by many relatives and friends. She enjoyed daily walks to Rockport Harbor, frequent visits to the top of Mount Battie and being a long-time member of the Mid Coast Community Chorus. She was always ready to go anywhere with anyone that wanted to travel. Over the next 15 years among other adventures she: walked the Great Wall in China, rode an elephant in Thailand, ziplined over Victoria Falls in Africa, did a train trip across Canada, rode a camel Tunisia, fed the macaques in Gibraltar, hiked the glaciers in Patagonia, visited the Winter Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia, cruised the Amazon in Brazil, visited the Wailing Wall in Jerusalem, hot air ballooned in Turkey, also toured Ireland, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Croatia, Finland, Estonia, Singapore, South Africa and many other destinations. She fulfilled her world travel bucket list except travel to Antarctica. Jojo was predeceased by her husband, Fred, in 2004; her daughter, Diana Hicks in 2013; and her grandson Andrew Hicks in 2010. She is survived by her son, Fred McAlary and his wife Mary of Andover, Massachusetts; grandson Ryan and his partner Phil Coppola of Haverhill, Massachusetts; son-in-law Tony Hicks, of Leesburg, Florida; granddaughter, Jennifer Hicks of Brunswick, Maine; grandson Andrew Hicks and his wife Karen of Annapolis, Maryland; as well as five great-grandchildren. two great-great grandchildren, and a nephew, David McAlary. A Memorial Service will be scheduled in August in Rockport, Maine. Further details will be forthcoming. Condolences and memories may be shared at www.longfuneralhomecamden.com. October 29, 2026, https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/khnp-ends-daewoodoosan-talks-on-187-billion-czech-nuclear-plant/12946437 Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP), Korea’s state-run nuclear power operator, said Thursday it has ended negotiations with a local consortium on a construction contract for a nuclear power plant project in the Czech Republic after the two sides failed to agree on key terms. “The company has decided to terminate negotiations with a consortium comprising Daewoo Engineering & Construction and Doosan Enerbility for the Dukovany nuclear power plant project. The breakdown is due to differences over key contract terms,” KHNP said in a press release. KHNP said it will formally conclude the negotiations and begin preparations for a tender to select a new contractor. “We aim to sign a contract with a new consortium for the Czech project during July of 2027,” Choi Il-kyung, executive vice president of KHNP’s overseas business division, said. The Dukovany project, valued at about 25 trillion won ($18.7 billion), involves the construction of two 1,000-megawatt APR1000 reactors, a Korean-designed model, in the Czech Republic. A Korean consortium led by KHNP won the project last year. KHNP subsequently negotiated a construction contract with the Daewoo-Doosan consortium, which had been designated as the construction contractor. “The end of the negotiations does not mean the overall nuclear power plant project has been canceled as KHNP is preparing follow-up measures,” the company said. The consortium expressed regret over KHNP’s decision, saying the nuclear operator had introduced revised contract terms in early October and rejected its request to extend the Thursday deadline before unilaterally ending negotiations. It argued that the revised terms would unfairly burden construction contractors with additional costs arising from design changes, despite their lack of involvement in the reactor’s design. It also accused KHNP of violating the principle of good faith by refusing further talks unless the consortium accepted the revised terms, urging the nuclear operator to resume negotiations in the broader national interest. In a Facebook post, Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said he respects KHNP’s decision and pledged government support for the successful construction of the nuclear power plant in the Czech Republic. https://www.g4media.ro/copil-de-9-ani-ra.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. Un copil de 9 ani a ajuns, duminică, la spital după ce o petardă i-a explodat în mână. Incidentul a avut loc în localitatea Cosoba, județul Giurgiu. Băiatul a ridicat de pe stradă o petardă neexplodată pentru a o reaprindă, moment în care aceasta i-ar fi explodat în mână. „La data de 15 noiembrie a.c., în jurul orei 14.00, polițiștii din cadrul Secției de Poliție Rurală nr. 3 Bolintin-Vale au fost sesizați, prin apel 112, de către un bărbat, din localitatea Cosoba, județul Giurgiu, cu privire la faptul că un copil s-ar fi rănit la mână cu o petardă”, anunță IPJ Giurgiu, conform Mediafax. Polițiștii au constatat că, în timp ce se aflau pe o stradă din localitatea Cosoba, mai mulți copii s-ar fi jucat cu materiale pirotehnice, iar la un moment dat, unul dintre ei, în vârstă de 9 ani, ar fi luat de jos o petardă neexplodată pentru a o reaprinde, moment în care aceasta ar fi explodat în mâna minorului. La fața locului a fost necesară intervenția unui echipaj medical care l-a transportat pe copil la o unitate spitalicească, din municipiul București, în vederea acordării de îngrijiri medicale de specialitate. „În cauză, a fost întocmit un dosar penal sub aspectul săvârșirii infracțiunilor de vătămare corporală din culpă și utilizarea fără drept a articolelor pirotehnice. Cercetările sunt continuate de către polițiști în vederea stabilirii întregii stări de fapt”, precizează polițiștii din Giurgiu.
